text:
jon: New hire hit onboarding snag: node sample tsc passes but the edge sample (Vite) fails in the browser with "module does not provide named export". Wrangler pack also errored on deploy.
peyton: what import style are they using?
jon: app does `import { createClient } from 'redwood-inference'`. Local node tests fine, but Vite dev server pulled a CJS entry and stripped named exports.
anya: likely export map ambiguity. Our package.json has ".": { "node": "./cjs/index.js", "default": "./esm/index.mjs" } but we don't expose "types" at top-level or under exports.
ci-bot: ci:pr #9999 vite-build: failed \u2014 found CJS entry in browser context causing named export mismatch.
sam-devex: Short checklist to fix:
- Add top-level "types": "./types/index.d.ts" so TS always finds defs.
- Add "types" condition to `exports` root and subpaths.
- Make `exports` explicit: "import": "./esm/index.mjs", "require": "./cjs/index.js", "node": "./cjs/index.js", and "default": "./esm/index.mjs".
peyton: Also add `module`/`main` fields for older tooling and a `browser`/`worker` condition for bundlers that look for them.
anya: CI: add `tsc --noEmit` for samples and a Vite build + wrangler pack step in PR checks to catch this before release.
jon: I patched the onboarding sample to explicitly import from `redwood-inference/esm/index.mjs` so the new hire can continue. Will revert after fix.
sam-devex: I'll open a tiny PR with the package.json changes + README note: avoid deep imports; use public entrypoints. Also add a troubleshooting snippet showing `npm pack` and `node -p require.resolve('redwood-inference')` to inspect what consumers get.
peyton: Nice. Please add a short blurb in release notes so downstream customers know to update bundler configs if needed.
jon: Filed issue #7744 and linked the sample patch. Thanks all.
